---
name: caveman
description: >
  Ultra-compressed communication mode. Cuts output tokens 65% (measured) by speaking like caveman
  while keeping full technical accuracy. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra,
  wenyan-lite, wenyan-full, wenyan-ultra.
  Use when user says "caveman mode", "talk like caveman", "use caveman", "less tokens",
  "be brief", or invokes /caveman. Also auto-triggers when token efficiency is requested.
---

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim â€” unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **lite** | No filler/hedging. Keep articles + full sentences. Professional but tight |
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |
| **ultra** | Strip conjunctions when cause-then-effect stay unambiguous. One word when one word enough. State each fact once. NO prose abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn/auth), NO arrows (X â†’ Y) â€” measured zero token saving under tokenizer, cost decode clarity. Code symbols, function names, API names, error strings: never touch |
| **wenyan-lite** | Semi-classical. Drop filler/hedging but keep grammar structure, classical register |
| **wenyan-full** | Maximum classical terseness. Fully æ–‡è¨€æ–‡. 80-90% character reduction. Classical sentence patterns, verbs precede objects, subjects often omitted, classical particles (ä¹‹/ä¹ƒ/ç‚º/å…¶) |
| **wenyan-ultra** | Extreme abbreviation while keeping classical Chinese feel. Maximum compression, ultra terse |

Example â€” "Why React component re-render?"
- lite: "Your component re-renders because you create a new object reference each render. Wrap it in `useMemo`."
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."
- ultra: "Inline obj prop, new ref, re-render. `useMemo`."

- lite: "Connection pooling reuses open connections instead of creating new ones per request. Avoids repeated handshake overhead."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` â€” order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example â€” destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

    drawing: Pick<DiagramGroupDrawingService, 'completeGroup'>
    onCancel: () => void

/** Required-label form mounted only while one completed rectangle awaits creation. */
export function DiagramGroupLabelForm({ drawing, onCancel }: DiagramGroupLabelFormProps) {
    const [label, setLabel] = useState('')
    const [validationError, setValidationError] = useState<string | null>(null)
    const handleLabelChange = (event: ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>) => setLabel(event.target.value)
    const handleSubmit = (event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => {
        event.preventDefault()
        if (label.trim().length === 0) {
            setValidationError('Label is required.')

            return
        }

        drawing.completeGroup(label)
    }

    return (
        <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
            <DialogContent dividers>

                    {validationError ? <Alert severity="error">{validationError}</Alert> : null}
                    <Typography color="text.secondary" variant="body2">Label</Typography>
                    <TextField
                        autoFocus
                        onChange={handleLabelChange}
                        required
                        size="small"
                        slotProps={{ htmlInput: { 'aria-label': 'Label' } }}
                        value={label}

                </Stack>
            </DialogContent>
            <DialogActions>
                <Button onClick={onCancel} variant="outlined">Cancel</Button>
                <Button type="submit" variant="contained">Save</Button>
            </DialogActions>
        </form>
    )
}

Need scope choice. Proposed behavior:

- Non-Ctrl node add: focus inline label; select default text.
- Non-Ctrl edge add: open Details dialog; focus/select Label.
- Ctrl continuous add: keep tool active; do not move focus.
- Group: existing pre-creation label focus unchanged.
- Fragment: excluded; no label.

Correct?

> Ctrl continuous add: keep tool active; do not move focus.

but the tool is just a selection mode that determines click behavior. can't we allow the user to type while still using ctrl when clicking?

Yes. Active Add tool and keyboard focus are independent state.

After Ctrl-click creates item:

- Keep Add tool active.
- Move focus to new label and select default text.
- User releases Ctrl, then types replacement label.
- Next surface click creates another item because Add tool remains active.

Only concern: typing while Ctrl remains physically held triggers browser/app shortcuts. Normal flow assumes Ctrl released after click. Revised design should support label focus for both single-add and continuous-add modes.

> typing while Ctrl remains physically held triggers browser/app shortcuts.

yes, we don't need to handle these. user must release ctrl key to type text. the list you made is correct. is this how it is implemented today? cause that is not how it is working.

No. Current code keeps Ctrl-add tool active, but never requests label focus after creation. Node and edge services only create item and select it. Non-Ctrl additionally switches tool to Select. Group label already receives focus before group creation; fragments have no label. Clarification resolved; updating feature doc with focus independent from tool state.

ctrl tab in dashboard view should switch between topmost popup.

## Current state

* "Dashboard view" is the cards workspace view (`WorkspaceViewMode` `cards`, see J_63).
* Popup stack: `CardPopupService` (`app/src/services/card_popup_service.ts`) owns an ordered `entries` list of three kinds: `action` (rendered by `CardActionPopupHost`), `card-details` (`CardBodyPopover`), and `sequence` (`CardSequenceDialog`). The last entry is the topmost popup; `stackPosition` (list index) sets the z-index in `ResizablePopper`. In cards view every entry is visible; on mobile width only the top entry is visible.
* `activate(id)` moves one entry to the end of the list and dispatches `changed`. It does not move keyboard focus. Clicking or focusing a popup calls `activate` through `ResizablePopper` `onActivate` (`onPointerDownCapture`, `onFocusCapture`).
* Focus: `ResizablePopper` focuses its paper (`role="dialog"`, `tabIndex={-1}`) only once, on first mount (`focusOnMountRef`, `setPaperElement`). No way exists to focus an already mounted popup from outside.
* Keyboard: `KeyboardShortcutService` routes keys to the global service, then the active view service. `cardsKeyboardShortcutService` (`app/src/services/shortcuts/cards_keyboard_shortcut_service.ts`) is a stub that handles nothing. `TextKeyboardShortcutService` already maps Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (`NEXT_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT`, `PREVIOUS_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` in `list_tab_shortcuts.ts`) to next and previous open document.
* No popup component handles Ctrl+Tab itself, so the key reaches the window listener.

## implementation details

* Behavior: in cards view, Ctrl+Tab cycles forward through the popup stack: the bottom-most popup moves to the top. Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycles backward: the top popup moves to the bottom. Repeated presses visit every popup. After each cycle, keyboard focus moves into the new top popup.
* `CardPopupService`:
  * New method `cycle(offset: 1 | -1)`. With fewer than two entries, return `false`. Forward: move `entries[0]` to the end. Backward: move the last entry to the front. Call `setEntries`, then dispatch a focus request for the new top entry, then return `true`.
  * Focus request is a granular event per entry: type `focusRequested:<entryId>` (constant prefix in the module). Order matters: entries update first, focus request second.
  * New exported function `subscribeCardPopupFocusRequest(entryId, listener)` next to `subscribeCardPopups`; returns an unsubscribe function.
* `CardsKeyboardShortcutService`: replace the stub object with a class like `TextKeyboardShortcutService`, with dependency `{ popups: CardPopupService }`. `handleKeyDown`: on `NEXT_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` return `popups.cycle(1)`; on `PREVIOUS_LIST_TAB_SHORTCUT` return `popups.cycle(-1)`; else `false`. Singleton passes `cardPopupService`. Only call site: `viewServices` in `keyboard_shortcut_service.ts` (unchanged import name).
* `ResizablePopper`: new optional prop `subscribeFocusRequest?: (listener: () => void) => () => void`. An effect subscribes when the prop is set. On request: if `paperRef.current` exists, focus it; else set `focusOnMountRef.current = true`, so the paper focuses when it mounts (mobile: new top popup opens only after the reorder renders). Other `ResizablePopper` users (search panel, file search menu, diagram popups) pass nothing; unchanged.
* Pass the subscription from each card popup owner, built with `useCallback` on `entry.id`:
  * `CardActionPopupHostEntry` to `ActionPopup` (new optional prop), into `ActionPopupContentProps`, then `ActionPopupFrame` to `ResizablePopper`. Diagram action popups pass nothing.
  * `CardBodyPopoverEntry` to its `ResizablePopper`.
  * `CardSequenceDialog` to its `ResizablePopper` (only when `entry` exists).
* Focus side effect: focusing the new top paper fires `onFocusCapture`, which calls `activate` on the entry that is already top; no-op, no extra `changed` event.
* Edge cases:
  * Zero or one popup: `cycle` returns `false`; key is not handled; nothing changes.
  * Other views: text view keeps its Ctrl+Tab document switching; diagrams and stats views unchanged (cards service not active there).
  * Focus inside a text field of the old top popup: Ctrl+Tab still cycles; focus leaves the field.
  * Modal MUI dialog open above popups (delete card, affects editor): popups still reorder beneath; the dialog focus trap keeps focus in the dialog.
* Tests:
  * `card_popup_service.test.ts`: forward and backward cycle order with three entries; focus request fires for the new top entry only, after `changed`; fewer than two entries returns `false` and dispatches nothing.
  * New `cards_keyboard_shortcut_service.node.test.ts` (popup service stub): Ctrl+Tab calls `cycle(1)`, Ctrl+Shift+Tab calls `cycle(-1)`, return value passes through; other keys return `false`.
  * `resizable_popper.test.tsx`: focus request focuses a mounted paper; request while closed focuses the paper after open.
  * Run those files directly and `npm run lint` in `app/`.

## acceptance criteria

1. In cards view with two or more popups open (any mix of action, card details, sequence), Ctrl+Tab brings the bottom-most popup to the top.
2. Repeated Ctrl+Tab visits every open popup in turn and returns to the first after a full cycle.
3. Ctrl+Shift+Tab cycles in the opposite direction: the top popup moves to the bottom.
4. After each Ctrl+Tab or Ctrl+Shift+Tab, keyboard focus is inside the new top popup, also on mobile width where only the top popup shows.
5. With zero or one popup, Ctrl+Tab changes nothing.
6. Ctrl+Tab in text view still switches open documents; diagrams and stats views are unchanged.
7. Ctrl+Tab handling lives in `CardsKeyboardShortcutService` and `CardPopupService`; no shortcut registration in `.tsx` files.

+
+## Current state
+
+* `DiagramAddControl` activates node placement, edge drawing, group drawing, or fragment creation. `DiagramZoomViewport` passes the pointer event's `ctrlKey` to node, edge, and group completion.
+* `DiagramNodePlacementService.place` and `DiagramEdgeDrawingService.completeTarget` create and select the new object. Without Ctrl they switch to Select; with Ctrl they keep the Add tool active. Neither path requests keyboard focus.
+* Editable nodes render their label through `DiagramInlineNodeControls`. Its `TextField` can edit the label, but has no focus request or input ref, so adding a node leaves focus outside the label.
+* Edges have no inline label input. Their label is edited in `DiagramEdgeDetailsEditor`, whose Label field receives focus only after the details dialog is opened manually.
+* Group drawing already opens `DiagramGroupLabelDialog` before creation. Its required Label field has `autoFocus`; saving that form creates the group. Sequence fragments have operators and region guards, but no label field.
+* Selection and active Add tool are independent view state. Keeping a node or edge Add tool active does not prevent focus from moving to the new object's label.
+
+## implementation details
+
+* Add `DiagramLabelFocusService` in `app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_label_focus_service.ts`. It owns one pending `{ objectId, objectKind }` target for `node` or `edge`, publishes changes through `EventTarget`, and exposes snapshot, subscription, request, and completion operations. A request remains pending until the matching input focuses, so creation and React mounting order cannot lose it. Clear pending state when the edit session changes.
+* Inject the focus service into `DiagramNodePlacementService` and `DiagramEdgeDrawingService`. After successful creation, selection, gesture completion, and any tool transition, request label focus for the returned ID. Request focus for both ordinary clicks and Ctrl-clicks. Ctrl affects only whether the Add tool remains active.
+* In `DiagramInlineNodeControls`, subscribe only to the focus state for its node. When requested, focus the underlying input, select its complete default label, then complete the request. Existing pointer-event isolation remains: typing edits the label while the active node Add tool still determines later surface-click behavior.
+* Add a small edge-focus handler under `components/diagram_view/editing`. When an edge focus request arrives, open `DiagramObjectDetailsService` for that edge. `DiagramEdgeDetailsEditor` then focuses and selects the complete Label value before completing the request. Manual details opening keeps its current focus behavior and must not be treated as a creation request.
+* Do not change Add-tool state when focusing. After Ctrl-click, user releases Ctrl and types; behavior while Ctrl remains physically held needs no special handling. After editing, the next diagram-surface click still uses the active Add tool.
+* Group creation remains unchanged because its label is already focused and entered before creation. Fragment creation remains unchanged because fragments have no label.
+* Cover focus-service request lifetime and session clearing; node and edge requests for Ctrl and non-Ctrl creation; node input focus and full-text selection; edge dialog opening, focus, and full-text selection; and preserved active-tool state after Ctrl creation. Run affected diagram service/component tests and `npm run lint` in `app/`.
+
+## acceptance criteria
+
+1. After adding a node without Ctrl, its inline Label input has keyboard focus and its complete default label is selected, so typing replaces that label.
+2. After adding an edge without Ctrl, its details dialog opens, its Label input has keyboard focus, and its complete default or existing label is selected.
+3. After adding a node or edge with Ctrl, the same label focus and selection occur while the chosen Add tool remains active.
+4. After a Ctrl-add, releasing Ctrl and typing changes only the new object's label. The next diagram-surface click still starts or completes another addition with the active tool.

+6. Group creation keeps focusing its required pre-creation Label field. Fragment creation remains unchanged because a fragment has no label.
+7. Manually opening node or edge details retains its current focus behavior; full-label selection caused by this feature occurs only for a newly added object.

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked â€” quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) â€” tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (â†’) either â€” own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese â†’ reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish â†’ reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only â€” never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

With the add tool, the user can add new items to a diagram. Most items have a label. Keyboard focus should be on this label after adding, so user can start typing label without extra clicking

## Current state

* `DiagramAddControl` activates node placement, edge drawing, group drawing, or fragment creation. `DiagramZoomViewport` passes the pointer event's `ctrlKey` to node, edge, and group completion.
* `DiagramNodePlacementService.place` and `DiagramEdgeDrawingService.completeTarget` create and select the new object. Without Ctrl they switch to Select; with Ctrl they keep the Add tool active. Neither path requests keyboard focus.
* Editable nodes render their label through `DiagramInlineNodeControls`. Its `TextField` can edit the label, but has no focus request or input ref, so adding a node leaves focus outside the label.
* Edges have no inline label input. Their label is edited in `DiagramEdgeDetailsEditor`, whose Label field receives focus only after the details dialog is opened manually.
* Group drawing already opens `DiagramGroupLabelDialog` before creation. Its required Label field has `autoFocus`; saving that form creates the group. Sequence fragments have operators and region guards, but no label field.
* Selection and active Add tool are independent view state. Keeping a node or edge Add tool active does not prevent focus from moving to the new object's label.

## implementation details

* Add `DiagramLabelFocusService` in `app/src/services/diagrams/diagram_label_focus_service.ts`. It owns one pending `{ objectId, objectKind }` target for `node` or `edge`, publishes changes through `EventTarget`, and exposes snapshot, subscription, request, and completion operations. A request remains pending until the matching input focuses, so creation and React mounting order cannot lose it. Clear pending state when the edit session changes.
* Inject the focus service into `DiagramNodePlacementService` and `DiagramEdgeDrawingService`. After successful creation, selection, gesture completion, and any tool transition, request label focus for the returned ID. Request focus for both ordinary clicks and Ctrl-clicks. Ctrl affects only whether the Add tool remains active.
* In `DiagramInlineNodeControls`, subscribe only to the focus state for its node. When requested, focus the underlying input, select its complete default label, then complete the request. Existing pointer-event isolation remains: typing edits the label while the active node Add tool still determines later surface-click behavior.
* Add a small edge-focus handler under `components/diagram_view/editing`. When an edge focus request arrives, open `DiagramObjectDetailsService` for that edge. `DiagramEdgeDetailsEditor` then focuses and selects the complete Label value before completing the request. Manual details opening keeps its current focus behavior and must not be treated as a creation request.
* Do not change Add-tool state when focusing. After Ctrl-click, user releases Ctrl and types; behavior while Ctrl remains physically held needs no special handling. After editing, the next diagram-surface click still uses the active Add tool.
* Group creation remains unchanged because its label is already focused and entered before creation. Fragment creation remains unchanged because fragments have no label.
* Cover focus-service request lifetime and session clearing; node and edge requests for Ctrl and non-Ctrl creation; node input focus and full-text selection; edge dialog opening, focus, and full-text selection; and preserved active-tool state after Ctrl creation. Run affected diagram service/component tests and `npm run lint` in `app/`.

## acceptance criteria

1. After adding a node without Ctrl, its inline Label input has keyboard focus and its complete default label is selected, so typing replaces that label.
2. After adding an edge without Ctrl, its details dialog opens, its Label input has keyboard focus, and its complete default or existing label is selected.
3. After adding a node or edge with Ctrl, the same label focus and selection occur while the chosen Add tool remains active.
4. After a Ctrl-add, releasing Ctrl and typing changes only the new object's label. The next diagram-surface click still starts or completes another addition with the active tool.
5. Focus is requested only after creation succeeds. Failed or cancelled creation neither opens edge details nor moves focus to a label.
6. Group creation keeps focusing its required pre-creation Label field. Fragment creation remains unchanged because a fragment has no label.
7. Manually opening node or edge details retains its current focus behavior; full-label selection caused by this feature occurs only for a newly added object.

# Architectural decisions

Project-wide decisions for MDÂ². The app is a Vite React web app in `app/`; `desktop/` is a separate Electron host that can load the website and expose local capabilities through preload bridges.

## File naming

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code files use lowercase snake_case names. | All code files in `app/src/` and `desktop/` use lowercase words separated by underscores, for example `github_auth_service.ts`, `project_workspace.tsx`, and `local_git_service.js`. Test files keep the same base name with `.test` before the extension, for example `github_auth_service.test.ts`. Exported symbols keep normal TypeScript/JavaScript casing such as `GithubAuthService`, `ProjectWorkspace`, and `useGithubAuth`. | A single file naming convention avoids mixed PascalCase, camelCase, and hyphenated filenames, and keeps imports predictable across Windows and case-sensitive environments. |

## Services and state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Global singleton services own domain state and logic. | Each domain is a class in `src/services/**`, instantiated once at module level and exported, for example `export const indexesService = new IndexesService()`. React components do not own domain state. | Keeps business logic out of components, testable without a DOM, and shared across windows/views without Redux, Zustand, or Context stores. |
| Service location follows usage scope. | If a service is specific to one UI element and used only there, place it beside that component. Generic or shared services, such as logging, database access, config, storage, or cross-screen domain logic, belong in `src/services/`. | Keeps component-owned behavior local while preserving `src/services/` for reusable application services. |
| Consumers use direct imports or the service injector. | Direct import when no import cycle exists; use `src/services/service_injector.js` when a cycle would occur. Every global singleton service registers itself in its constructor with `inj.register('myService', this)`. | The service graph is dense; the injector is a bare global registry that defers resolution to call time. |
| Services have a two-phase lifecycle. | Constructors only register and set unloaded state such as `null`. Config-dependent or service-dependent work runs in `init()`, `start()`, app bootstrap (`App.jsx`), or a `loaded` lifecycle event. `configService.config` is private; callers use `get`, `set`, and `clear`. | Module evaluation order is not guaranteed, so `configService` is not usable at import time. Reading config in a constructor is a bug. |

## Card state

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The application has one `Card` domain type. | Do not create separate canonical, project, snapshot, or editor card types. The card-owning service holds the loaded cards and exposes focused operations that change only the requested field. React snapshots and editor drafts are read values; they must never replace or merge a complete card. Parser bookkeeping may remain private persistence metadata, but it is not another card model. | One card concept gives state a clear owner and prevents stale copies from overwriting newer worktree, activity, ordering, policy, or body values. |
| Card UI subscribes at field level. | A component subscribes only to the primitive or stable reference it renders, using granular `EventTarget` events and `useSyncExternalStore`. Do not clone or stringify a complete card to detect a field change. Group fields only in a deliberately small, stable projection when they are always rendered together. | A one-field change allocates and rerenders only what consumes that field, keeping memory use bounded and the UI responsive. |
| Cards are serialized only at persistence boundaries. | Mutate the owned `Card` through a focused operation, then serialize its current state when the persistence batch flushes. Editor changes update only the edited field. Activity linking updates only activity references. External file changes are parsed and applied deliberately without replacing dirty local state. | Persistence remains deterministic while concurrent saves and external updates cannot discard unrelated newer values. |


## Events and React integration

| Decision | Rule | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Services notify observers through their own `EventTarget`. | Services expose an `EventTarget` and dispatch named `CustomEvent` domain events such as `activeIndex`, `added`, `deleted`, or `changedBox`. Observers subscribe with `addEventListener` and unsubscribe with `removeEventListener` on the owning service. | Decouples producers from consumers without depending on Node `EventEmitter`, which is not available in the browser-first React app. |
| Custom hooks bridge service events to functional components. | Hooks in `src/components/hooks/`, such as `useActiveIndex` and `useProjectConfig`, seed `useState` from a service property, subscribe in `useEffect`, unsubscribe in cleanup, and return the value. Prefer hook + service over prop chains. | Components stay declarative and avoid direct event plumbing. |
| Components subscribe at the smallest rendering boundary. | Root and layout components compose UI regions and pass structural inputs. Components that render changing application data subscribe through hooks themselves. # App Style Guide â€” Kanban / MDÂ² (React + MUI)

How to build **any new component** so it matches the app. This is written for **Material UI v5+** components.

**The theme is the source of truth.** All color, radius, base typography, and spacing units live in the single `createTheme` (defined in `GUIDANCE.md` Â§1/Â§9). This guide does **not** define colors â€” it tells you **which theme value to use for which role**, and covers the things the theme can't encode: layout, spacing/margins, borders, elevation, and component conventions.

**The one rule that matters:** never write a raw hex, px radius, or magic color into a component. Read it from the theme (`theme.palette.*`, `theme.shape`, `theme.typography`, `theme.spacing`). If a component has a hardcoded hex in its `sx`/styled, it's wrong â€” that's exactly where the look drifts and where dark mode breaks.

---

## 1. How to consume the theme

- **Colors:** `sx={{ color: 'text.secondary', bgcolor: 'background.paper', borderColor: 'divider' }}` â€” MUI resolves dotted palette paths automatically in `sx`. In `styled`/JS use the callback form: `styled(Box)(({ theme }) => ({ color: theme.palette.text.secondary }))`.
- **Spacing:** use the 8px unit via the spacing scale â€” `sx={{ p: 2, gap: 1, mt: 1.5 }}` (`2` = 16px, `1` = 8px). Don't write `padding: '16px'`.
- **Radius:** `borderRadius: 1` (= `theme.shape.borderRadius` = 8) and multiples; for the fixed non-8 radii see Â§4.
- **Typography:** prefer `Typography variant=...` and `theme.typography.*` over ad-hoc `fontSize`.
- **Custom tokens:** roles the default MUI palette doesn't cover (column/track surfaces, the strong/hover border steps, `text-3/4`, section-header color, `primary-bg` tint, status colors) must exist in the theme under a namespace (e.g. `theme.palette.custom.*`) with light + dark values. Consume them the same way â€” `bgcolor: 'custom.column'`. **Never inline their hex.** If a needed token doesn't exist yet, add it to the theme, don't hardcode it in the component.

---

## 2. Role â†’ theme slot

Pick the slot by the element's **role**, not by how it looks in one mode:

| Role | Theme slot |
|---|---|
| App background; tinted footer/action bars | `background.default` |
| Column & sidebar surface | `custom.column` |
| Segmented-control / toolbar track, hover fill | `custom.track` |
| Card, dialog, popup, input surface | `background.paper` |
| Hairlines, resting borders | `divider` |
| Input borders, vertical separators | `custom.borderStrong` |
| Border on hover | `custom.borderHover` |
| Titles, values, headings | `text.primary` |
| Body copy, field labels | `text.secondary` |
| Meta, captions, resting icons | `custom.text3` |
| Muted / placeholder / disabled | `custom.text4` |
| Uppercase section/column headers | `custom.colHead` |
| The one CTA, selection, focus, links, icon-hover | `primary.main` |
| Contained-button hover | `primary.dark` |
| Selected/tinted bg, focus ring, ID-chip bg | `custom.primaryBg` |
| Text/icon on a primary fill | `primary.contrastText` |
| Active / saved / online dot | `success.main` |
| Destructive action | `error.main` |
| Status swatch dots & ID-chip tints (decorative only) | `custom.status.*` |

Rules: **one** `primary` per surface (the CTA/selection accent) â€” everything else is `text-*`/`divider`. Status colors are **decoration only** (dots, chip tints), never interactive color. Dark-mode brightness/tinting is handled inside the theme's two palettes, so a correctly-sloted component needs zero per-mode code.

---

## 3. Layout

- **Full-height app:** column flex â€” menu row / ribbon / content (`flex: 1; minHeight: 0`) / status bar. Fixed bands `flexShrink: 0`.
- **Board:** horizontal-scroll flex row, `gap: 2` (16px), page padding `p: 2.5` (20px); columns `width: 296, flexShrink: 0`, internal column flex `gap: 1`.
- **List view:** two-pane flex row filling the space between ribbon and status bar â€” sidebar `width: 280, flexShrink: 0`, editor pane `flex: 1, minWidth: 0` (the `minWidth: 0` is required 
[3715 characters omitted]
’ hover `borderColor/color: primary.main`. Destructive: hover `borderColor: error.main` + `bgcolor: custom.dangerBg`.
- **Contained (primary) CTA:** `primary.main` + small shadow â†’ hover `primary.dark`.
- **Input/field focus:** `borderColor: primary.main` + `boxShadow: 0 0 0 3px` in `custom.primaryBg` (the soft halo). Unfocused hover: `borderColor: custom.borderHover`.
- **List/tree row:** hover `bgcolor: track`; selected `bgcolor: custom.primaryBg` + title `text.primary`.
- **Row-level actions** (delete, â‹®): hidden at rest, shown on `:hover`/`:focus-within` via **opacity** (keep in DOM so width doesn't jump).
- **Active tab/menu item:** 2px `primary.main` bottom border + `primary.main` text.
- Every icon-only control gets a `Tooltip` (theme sets `arrow: true`) **and** an `aria-label`.

---

## 8. Component conventions (MUI primitives)

- **Buttons:** `Button variant="contained"` = the single CTA per surface; `variant="outlined"` = secondary; `variant="text"` = tertiary. Icon-only â†’ `IconButton` in a `Tooltip`. Don't use `Link` or text `Button` where an action button belongs (that reproduces the old text-link look).
- **Icons:** `@mui/icons-material` **Outlined** variants; `fontSize: 18` in 34px buttons, `16` in dense, `13â€“15` inline. Don't hand-draw SVG.
- **ID chip:** monospace, accent text on `custom.primaryBg`/status tint, `radius 5, flexShrink: 0`.
- **Count chip:** `background.paper` bg, 1px `divider`, radius 9â€“10, `custom.text3`.
- **State dot:** 7â€“8px circle + `text-3` label; green (`success.main`) = active/saved/online.
- **Search:** pill `TextField` (`borderRadius: 99`, `bgcolor: background.default`), search start-adornment, `âŒ˜K` keycap end-adornment.
- **Select:** `size="small"`, optional dot+name via `renderValue`; 42px / radius-9 frame. When a select has a tooltip, keep the tooltip available while the select is closed and explicitly hide it for the entire time the select menu is open so it cannot cover the first option.
- **Menu / context menu:** all `Menu` / `MenuItem` dropdowns and right-click context menus are dense by default through the theme. Call sites must not set density; `Select` option lists inherit the same density.
- **Segmented control** (view switch, formatting toolbar): `ToggleButtonGroup` on a `custom.track` background; selected segment `background.paper` + `0 1px 2px` shadow + `primary` text.
- **Dialog / popup:** `Dialog`/`Popover` with `PaperProps` â†’ `background.paper`, 1px `divider`, radius 14, big shadow; scrim via `slotProps.backdrop` (blur + tint). Bands separated by hairlines; footer on a `background.default` bar with top hairline; actions right-aligned (outlined Cancel + contained CTA). `autoFocus` first field; submit on `Enter` (`âŒ˜/Ctrl+Enter` in a textarea); close on `Esc`/backdrop â€” except that a dialog holding unsaved multi-field input may refuse `backdropClick` (return early from `onClose(event, reason)`) so a stray click on the scrim cannot discard typed values; `Esc` and the Cancel button must still close it, and Cancel stays visible and enabled, including while loading.
- **Empty state:** dashed target â€” `1.5px dashed custom.borderStrong`, radius 10, centered icon + `custom.text4` label. No "click to add" placeholder blocks.

---

## 9. Definition of done for a new component

1. Zero hardcoded hex / raw px colors â€” every value comes from `theme.palette` / `theme.shape` / `theme.spacing` / `theme.typography`.
2. Correct roleâ†’slot mapping (Â§2); at most one `primary` CTA on the surface.
3. Borders at rest, shadow only when floating (Â§5); bands split by a single hairline.
4. Hover **and** focus states on every interactive element (Â§7); icon buttons have tooltip + `aria-label`.
5. Body scrolls, header/footer pinned; `minWidth: 0` on flex children that hold long text.
6. Toggle to dark mode and confirm nothing breaks â€” if it does, you hardcoded a color somewhere (Â§1).

Component-specific detail lives in `GUIDANCE.md` (theme definition + board/list/dialog), `CARD_POPUP_GUIDE.md`, `RUN_DIALOG_GUIDE.md`, and `SIDEBAR_ACTIONS_GUIDE.md`.
